note: Every path the cert loop serves is pinned here with the digest it must have, so run_waves.sh resolves operands at run time instead of trusting a path that happens to exist. .gitignore excludes *.gguf, so the three ggufs below live in the clone's working tree and are not tracked; the JSON pins their bytes and sha256 instead.

model.name: openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B
model.scope: text backbone only; the vision tower and merger are never captured, edited or served
model.provenance: verification/minicpm-v47/summary.json (model block) + config.json read on this box

artifact_under_cert.role: base gguf and merge input (Q4_K_M export of the text backbone)
artifact_under_cert.verified: sha256 recomputed on this box on 2026-11-24; matches export_round_trip in verification/minicpm-v47/summary.json
artifact_under_cert.git: untracked by design (.gitignore: *.gguf); present in the clone, not a commit object

siblings.note: committed alongside the Q4_K_M export; not the cert artifact
committed alongside the Q4_K_M export; not the cert artifact

axis.why: no capture (records .pt) of this lineage exists on this box: the searched paths hold only a unit-random probe axis from the merge dry-run, and a unit-random axis is a merge-path probe, never a fit
axis.capture: uv run jdewitt capture --model <HF_MODEL> --revision <HF_REVISION> --suite verification/p7-minicpm/fit-suite.jsonl --gguf <base> --out <records.pt> --ctx-size 4096 --kinds refusal,harmless --locus answer
axis.fit: uv run python -m jdewitt.spanfit axes --records <records.pt> --out <axes.pt> --shape perlayer
axis.scale_note: scale is a search variable; this card ships the pipeline at 1.0 (full axis removal). The wave card may sweep SCALE without changing the script.
axis.labelled_refit: the packet's artifact recipe carries edit text naming this a REFIT and the fit suite's sha256, so no reader can mistake it for a rebuild from a saved capture
axis.capture_device: B70 XPU (jdewitt.capture refuses CPU by design); this prep card does not run it

merge_probe.what: the CPU merge path was exercised on this exact gguf with a unit-random probe axis before this card: 672,004,000 bytes merged in 56.6 s, all 48 discovered residual-write tensors visited
merge_probe.proves: targets discovery, axis-space output and the writer work on this artifact
merge_probe.does_not_prove: any fit; the axis was random and the output was never served

fit.rule: 40 refusal rows (8 families x 5) + 20 harmless rows; recut by verification/p7-minicpm/recut_suites.py

held_out.rule: 24 families x 5 rows, disjoint from advbench-40; recut by verification/p7-minicpm/recut_suites.py

suites.disjointness: no prompt id and no prompt text appears in two pools: checked by recut_suites.py overlap_checks at every run

tools.server_note: the CPU build this model was served with in verification/minicpm-v47/serving-check.json; DEVICE_ARGS defaults to --device none. A Vulkan server may be substituted by the wave card (SERVER / DEVICE_ARGS) and the argv is recorded in every wave + the packet (R9)
tools.merge: uv run python -m jdewitt.spanfit build --axes ... --gguf-targets auto
tools.fidelity: uv run python scripts/p4f_gate.py fidelity (compare_edit, full-tensor decode)
tools.config_pair: uv run python scripts/cert_config_pair.py (R9.4 boundary rows)

targets_discovered.note: read on this box; the merge refuses if the axes width and the artifact disagree, so a stale path cannot silently edit part of the model

caps.note: llama.cpp -c is the TOTAL context and --parallel splits it, so a request at 4096/4 can generate at most 1024 tokens. The comparison run is 2048/2 (also 1024 per slot) so the R9 pair differs only in ctx/parallel. The release matrix's registered cap floors for removal/held_out are 4096 (they were graded on a 8192/2 config); at the pinned 4096/4 this lineage cannot reach them and the analysis card must record that as a manifest decision, not paper over it
